title: Exception tracebacks can retain failed-initialization sockets until collection
applies_when: A Python resource constructor creates a real descriptor, then setup or connection fails before ownership transfers to a stream or pool; a leak hypothesis relies only on a missing close or a fake object's close counter.
lesson: Exercise the real native resource and public caller. Separate discarded errors, retained exception tracebacks, explicit GC and releasing those exceptions. Tracebacks keep frame locals alive: a socket retained there can remain open even after its surrounding pool exits, yet become collectable later. This supports prompt-failure-cleanup, not an uncollectable-leak claim. Pair failure-path explicit close plus unchanged exception mapping with successful ownership transfer. Inspect actual fileno or process FD counts, including a healthy control, and test the same regression against unchanged source and the proposed repair. Do not close a resource after it has been transferred to its successful caller.
avoid_when: Do not generalize CPython/Linux descriptor timing to every interpreter, platform or transport. A deliberate retained-error stress case is not evidence of typical production retention, descriptor exhaustion, throughput or permanent leakage. Runtime generation claims also need evidence: HTTPcore's _backends/sync.py is hand-maintained; unasync's _async to _sync target does not include it. Native validation and a published Discussion do not establish maintainer acceptance or complete CI.

evidence.note: Pinned backend creates a socket before option/connect steps and transfers it to SyncStream only on success; post-creation failure lacks explicit close. Source mechanism, not a measured production frequency.

Public Linux/Python3.12 reproduction retains 32 descriptors with 32 public-pool errors, then returns to baseline after errors are released and collected. Local native repair comparison reports four failures/two successes versus six successes, with real Unix/TCP success controls. Discussion is a proposal, not an accepted patch.
The generator's actual source/target directories distinguish generated _sync modules from the independent _backends/sync.py file.
